assertions.text: The note is a file under notes/ named YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md, the slug three words at most
assertions.evidence: The run added `notes/2026-10-08-search-index-postgresql.md`. The date matches today (2026-10-08) and the slug `search-index-postgresql` is three words.

assertions.text: The note opens with a frontmatter holding status: draft
assertions.evidence: The file opens with `# Move the search index to PostgreSQL`, then `Date: 2026-10-08`. There is no `---` frontmatter block and no `status: draft`.

assertions.text: The note's first line is its `# ` title
assertions.evidence: Line 1 is `# Move the search index to PostgreSQL`.

assertions.text: The note closes with a ## Next section that names Alice and the schema migration
assertions.evidence: The last section is headed `## Next steps`, not `## Next`. It does end the file and contains `- Alice migrates the schema next week (week of 2026-10-12).`, so Alice and the schema migration are named. The required `## Next` heading is not there.

assertions.text: Each line of the ## Next section opens with who does it, then a colon, as `Alice: …`
assertions.evidence: The section is `## Next steps`; its line `- Alice migrates the schema next week (week of 2026-10-12).` opens with Alice, but no colon follows the name.

assertions.text: No file is written outside notes/

claims.evidence: The file exists in outputs/notes and changes.json lists it as added.

claims.claim: The repo was empty, so there were no existing conventions.
claims.evidence: The first `ls` showed only `.git`, and the git log showed a single commit, `base`.

claims.claim: "Next week" was turned into "week of 2026-10-12", and that week starts on Monday the 12th.
claims.evidence: The note contains `(week of 2026-10-12)`. 2026-10-08 is a Thursday, so 2026-10-12 is the following Monday.

claims.claim: The note has the decision, the reason, and the next step (Alice migrates the schema next week).
claims.evidence: The note has `## Decision`, `## Why` and `## Next steps` sections with that content.

claims.claim: It added nothing beyond what the user said: no store name, no decision-maker, no deadline.
claims.evidence: The note names no store, decision-maker or deadline. The only additions are the date header and the week-of date.

claims.claim: The file is untracked on `master` and was not committed.
claims.evidence: No commit was made, which is consistent with the transcript. The run never ran `git status` or checked the branch name, so "untracked on `master`" is not shown by anything in the transcript.
